ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatial and focal branches fused for indoor depth from focus
PROPOSAL: Train a two-branch network on the DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 focal stacks. A spatial branch encodes structure across neighbouring pixels with learned gradient filters, and a focal branch encodes each pixel's sharpness profile across slices with a one-dimensional convolution. A fusion head outputs a depth map and a confidence map. Optimise with AdamW, a batch of 8, an L1 depth loss and an edge-aware smoothness term. Report RMSE, absolute relative error, the fraction of pixels within a factor 1.25 of the reference depth, and an edge F-score around depth discontinuities.
CONTROLS: Compare against the published DFV network and a Laplacian-variance focus measure on identical focal stacks with the same crop. Compare against a variant that feeds the stack as generic channels with the same parameter count. Compare edge accuracy on textured patches against depth-discontinuity patches under the same evaluation mask. Repeat training with five seeds and report the spread of every metric.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Expect lower RMSE and sharper edges than the published DFV network, with the largest gains in low-texture regions. The claim fails if the gain vanishes on reflective surfaces or if the edge F-score does not improve over the generic-channel variant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Structure and focus streams combined to refine indoor depth maps
PROPOSAL: Build a dual-stream model trained on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 stacks. A structure stream applies learned derivative filters over adjacent pixels while a focus stream runs a one-dimensional convolution along the slice axis for every pixel; a fusion head predicts depth together with an uncertainty map. Training relies on AdamW, a batch of 8, an L1 loss on depth and an edge-aware smoothness penalty. Evaluation covers RMSE, absolute relative error, the share of pixels within a factor 1.25 of the reference depth, and an edge F-score near depth discontinuities.
CONTROLS: Compare against a published monocular depth network and a Sobel edge detector on identical all-in-focus images with the same crop. Compare against a variant with a wider backbone with the same slice count. Compare edge accuracy on bright patches against dark patches under the same evaluation mask. Repeat training with five seeds and report the spread of every metric.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Expect lower RMSE and sharper edges than the published monocular network, with the largest gains in low-texture regions. The claim fails if the gain vanishes on reflective surfaces or if the edge F-score does not improve over the wider variant.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Thin-lens sharpness curves for depth from sparse focal stacks
PROPOSAL: Predict, for every pixel, the parameters of a thin-lens sharpness curve over focus distance and read depth from the curve peak. A ResNet-34 encoder with a feature pyramid takes each slice, a transformer layer mixes information along the slice axis, and a head regresses curve centre and width. Train on DDFF 12-Scene with an L1 depth loss and a curve-fit loss, using AdamW and a batch of 8. Evaluate RMSE and absolute relative error on the held-out scenes when the stack is subsampled to 3, 5 and 10 slices.
CONTROLS: Compare the curve-peak depth with the argmax-over-slices depth from the same network features. Vary the number of input slices while the training schedule is held fixed. Add Gaussian noise at matched levels to every stack and compare errors with the reference run. Repeat evaluation on a held-out scene split with five seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Expect the curve-peak readout to degrade more slowly than the argmax readout as slices are removed. It is refuted if the gap closes under noise or if the error with 3 slices is not below the argmax error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Curve-based depth readout with a lightweight convolutional encoder
PROPOSAL: Regress per-pixel sharpness curves over focus distance and take depth at the curve maximum. A ResNet-34 trunk with a feature pyramid processes every slice, one attention layer exchanges information across slices, and a prediction head returns curve centre and width. Training uses DDFF 12-Scene, an L1 depth loss plus a curve-fit loss, AdamW and a batch of 8. Report RMSE and absolute relative error on held-out scenes for stacks subsampled to 3, 5 and 10 slices.
CONTROLS: Compare the curve-peak depth with the depth from the same network features after a colour-space change. Vary the augmentation strength while the training schedule is held fixed. Add shifted crops at matched positions to every stack and compare errors with the reference run. Repeat evaluation on a held-out scene split with five seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Expect the curve-peak readout to degrade more slowly than a plain maximum readout as slices are removed. It is refuted if the gap closes under augmentation or if the error with 3 slices is not below the colour-space error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Metric depth from a relative-depth prior and a focal stack
PROPOSAL: Start from a frozen Depth Anything V2 model that outputs relative depth for the middle slice, and fuse it with a lightweight focal encoder that supplies metric scale through sharpness peaks. A cross-attention module lets prior features query focal features, and a scale head regresses a per-pixel scale and shift. Fine-tune on DDFF 12-Scene indoor stacks with an L1 loss and a gradient-matching loss, AdamW, and a batch of 4. Report RMSE and absolute relative error, split by region type.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on low-texture and reflective regions defined by a local variance mask. Compare against the relative-depth prior with a global scale-and-shift fitted to the reference depth. Subsample the stack to five slices and compare with the full stack under the same schedule. Repeat on stacks from a second camera with five seeds.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Expect the largest gain over the prior in reflective and low-texture regions, where relative depth is least reliable. The claim fails if the fused model matches the scale-and-shift fit there, or if the error rises sharply on the second camera.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focal-stack refinement of a pretrained relative-depth network
PROPOSAL: Attach a small focal encoder to a frozen Depth Anything V2 network, which reads the central slice only. The encoder turns sharpness peaks into metric scale, and a cross-attention module lets the network's features query it before a scale head returns per-pixel scale and shift. Fine-tuning uses indoor DDFF 12-Scene stacks, an L1 loss with a gradient-matching term, AdamW and a batch of 4. RMSE and absolute relative error are broken down by region type.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on high-texture and matte regions defined by a local variance mask. Compare against the relative-depth prior with a global scale-and-shift fitted to the reference depth. Subsample the stack to nine slices and compare with the full stack under the same schedule. Repeat on stacks from the same camera with five seeds.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Expect a clear gain over the prior in matte and high-texture regions, where fused depth should look cleaner. The claim fails if the fused model matches the scale-and-shift fit there, or if the error rises sharply on the nine-slice stacks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-slice gradient consistency to separate texture from depth edges
PROPOSAL: Add a consistency module to a depth-from-focus network. A depth discontinuity shifts the gradient direction between slices as blur grows, whereas a surface pattern keeps its position. The module compares gradient maps from adjacent slices, produces an edge-likelihood map, and gates the smoothness term with it. Train on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 with an L1 loss, AdamW and a batch of 8. Report RMSE, absolute relative error, and edge precision and recall.
CONTROLS: Measure edge precision and recall of the predicted depth map against depth discontinuities in the ground truth, using the same tolerance in pixels. Compare on a texture-swapped test set in which printed patterns are applied to flat surfaces. Report the false-edge rate at textured but flat locations for the gated and ungated models. Repeat training with five seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Expect fewer false edges on textured flat surfaces and higher edge precision at similar recall. The result is refuted if the false-edge rate is unchanged after gating, or if recall drops by more than a few points.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-aware smoothness gating for focal-stack depth networks
PROPOSAL: Extend a depth-from-focus network with a gating module. Gradient maps taken from neighbouring slices are compared, an edge-likelihood map is predicted from their differences, and this map modulates the smoothness term during training. The backbone is a 3D encoder-decoder trained on DDFF 12-Scene and FoD500 with an L1 loss, AdamW and a batch of 8. Evaluation reports RMSE, absolute relative error, and the precision and recall of predicted edges.
CONTROLS: Measure gradient magnitude of the predicted depth map against gradient magnitude of the all-in-focus image, using the same tolerance in pixels. Compare on a brightness-shifted test set in which exposure changes are applied to flat surfaces. Report the mean absolute error over all pixels for the gated and ungated models. Repeat training with five seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Expect closer agreement in gradient magnitude and lower pixel error under gating. The result is refuted if the error is unchanged after gating, or if the agreement drops by more than a few points.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint spatial-focal attention for robust focal-stack depth
PROPOSAL: Replace generic 3D convolutions with factorised attention: spatial attention within each slice, then focal attention along the slice axis at every pixel, used in four blocks with a shared positional encoding for slice index. Train on DDFF 12-Scene with a combined L1 and scale-invariant loss, AdamW and a batch of 8. Report RMSE, absolute relative error and edge F-score, and show qualitative maps for fine-textured scenes and abrupt depth changes.
CONTROLS: Compare the joint model against a spatial-only variant and a focal-only variant, each with matched parameters. Evaluate each variant on fine-textured and abrupt-depth-change regions using the same masks. Vary the number of slices for every variant while the learning rate is held fixed. Repeat training with five seeds.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Expect the joint model to lead on fine textures and abrupt changes, with a smaller gain elsewhere. The claim fails if either single-branch variant matches the joint model on those regions, or if the ranking flips across seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Factorised attention blocks over image and focus axes
PROPOSAL: Swap generic 3D convolutions for two-stage attention: one stage attends across pixels of a single slice, the next attends along the slice axis for each pixel, stacked in four blocks that share a slice-index positional encoding. Training uses DDFF 12-Scene, a combined L1 and scale-invariant loss, AdamW and a batch of 8. Metrics are RMSE, absolute relative error and edge F-score, with qualitative maps for fine-textured scenes and abrupt depth changes.
CONTROLS: Compare the joint model against a spatial-only variant doubled in depth and a variant with the block order swapped, each with matched parameters. Evaluate each variant on image-centre and image-border regions using the same masks. Vary the weight decay for every variant while the learning rate is held fixed. Repeat training with five seeds.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Expect the joint model to lead on image-centre regions and to keep that lead on image-border regions. The claim fails if the depth-doubled variant matches the joint model there, or if the ranking flips across seeds.
